## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kūṭavāṇijajātaka* (Ja 218) is a birth story belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection. Set during the Buddha's residence at Jetavana, the story was delivered in connection with a dishonest trader [Fausböll 1879]. It opens with the verse incipit *saṭhassa sāṭheyyam idaṁ* [Fausböll 1879].

In the narrative of the past, two merchants of Sāvatthi—a dishonest trader (*kūṭavāṇija*) and a wise trader (*paṇḍitavāṇija*)—engage in commerce together [Fausböll 1879]. When ploughshares are stolen, the cheat fabricates an excuse that mice had consumed the iron implements; in retribution, the partner carries off the thief's son and alleges that a hawk had snatched the child away [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1879]. Brought to justice, each party is compelled to return what was taken—the lost son and the ploughshares [Fausböll 1879]. Concluding the story (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the dishonest trader and the wise merchant as their present counterparts, while the judge (*vinicchayamacca*) was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879].
